source.title: Windows PowerShell 5.1
source.versionPolicy: Windows PowerShell 5.1 as shipped with supported Windows releases; module and operating-system dependencies are recorded per document.

notes: The shell manual is original project text synthesized from the listed official topics rather than a copy of one upstream page.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 runtime evidence covers object flow, native text boundaries, no-clobber behavior, and the fact that uncaptured .NET/cmdlet success results contaminate enclosing output unless precisely captured or suppressed.

Corrected the built-in Certificate provider drive spelling from Certificate: to Cert: and distinguished provider name from drive name using official about_Providers plus dual-edition runtime evidence.
The reader-visible Runtime evidence section records the bounded 62-check Windows PowerShell 5.1 suite and leaves third-party, remote, and host-specific behavior outside that evidence.
This document is the navigation index; pwsh51.md is the primary shell and language manual.
Runtime verification belongs to the linked command, language, and compatibility pages; the navigation index itself introduces no separate shell behavior.
This is an original launcher guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

The installed Windows PowerShell 5.1 launcher accepted Version 5.1 first and started 5.1.26100.8875; a fixed literal Command source preserved child-side variable parsing. Stdin, encoded command, policy, apartment, host, profile, and failure-exit combinations remain outstanding.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 smoke verification covers the parsing examples. Local catalog harnesses demonstrated two whitespace failures: variable/parameter merging can fail a read before plausible downstream null/default counts, while Where-Object document-eq$name remains syntactically valid but silently selects zero rows. The page now requires explicit predicates, fail-fast reads, and expected coverage invariants.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed indexed interpolation versus subexpression selection, invariant interpolation versus de-DE ToString conversion with culture restoration, and a literal child-command source boundary. Here-strings, smart quotes, target-native parsers, Unicode, and other nested hosts remain outstanding.
No official about_Native_Commands topic exists in the locked 5.1 PowerShell-Docs baseline; this original guide is a project topic name informed by about_Parsing.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed alias-versus-executable resolution, native exit code 7, and the edition-specific 2>&1 NativeCommandError boundary under stopping versus scoped Continue error policy. Target quoting, stdin encoding, other tools, and Windows builds remain outstanding.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 parser evidence on 2026-08-12 confirmed that a bare foreach statement before a pipe raises EmptyPipeElement, while array/subexpression wrapping and an invoked script block each pass the two emitted objects to Measure-Object.

A ManT-result audit falsely counted one diagnostic because an omitted optional property produced null and @($null) is a one-element array. Windows PowerShell 5.1 confirmed wrapped=1, direct null Count=0, and a property/value-gated count=0; the page now makes this Agent evidence boundary searchable.

Runtime metadata and the official New-Item reference confirm Path exists but LiteralPath does not. The corrected output-suppression example uses -Path and requires target validation; the smoke suite locks this distinction.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows confirmed UTF-16LE redirection defaults, UTF-8 BOM output for Set-Content -Encoding UTF8, bounded no-clobber behavior, BOM-less UTF-8 misdecoding, native exit-code handling, and mixed-stream capture.

A 2026-08-12 isolated cmd.exe probe wrote one stderr line and returned 7. With ErrorActionPreference Stop and 2>&1, Windows PowerShell 5.1 entered catch with NativeCommandError before the assignment completed; LASTEXITCODE observed in that early catch varied between isolated and full-suite runs and is not reliable. A scoped Continue capture completed with one ErrorRecord and exit 7. No file or system state changed.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.
The page now indexes all 42 automatic variables listed in the locked Windows PowerShell 5.1 source rather than only the original common subset.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 in a clean NoProfile process confirmed the Desktop runtime variables, a present empty ConsoleFileName, absent PSDebugContext outside debugging, retained Matches data after a failed match, foreach and switch enumerators, legacy question-mark wrapper reset, native exit status, and missing Platform/OS version-table keys. Event, remoting, debugger, nested-prompt, psc1, Nano Server, and IoT contexts remain outstanding.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 in a clean NoProfile process confirmed that PROFILE is a string equal to CurrentUserCurrentHost and exposes all four documented profile-path properties. No profile file was read or created; loading order, host behavior, policy, remoting, and other configurations remain outstanding.
This is an original ManT-oriented topic guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed advanced-function begin/process/end timing and that an unsuppressed collection Add return value contaminates normal output. The probe used only in-memory values.
This is an original ManT-oriented cmdlet guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 in a clean NoProfile process confirmed alias precedence over a same-name function, ordered All results, and a nonempty Syntax view. The suite also checks core command, alias, and documented-option metadata; module, provider, PATH, and other-build variance remains outstanding.

The dual-edition NoProfile provider fixture passes 14/14: fixed built-in paths return the documented provider object types; FileSystem, Registry, and Certificate expose different dynamic parameters; Get-Help -Path Cert:\ returns provider-customized help; and Get-PSDrive can change later provider discovery by loading Microsoft.PowerShell.Security. It emits no environment value, registry data, certificate, or user path and performs no provider mutation or network access.
This is an original ManT-oriented cmdlet guide, not a copy of the upstream reference.

The probe performed no update, GUI, network, or profile-content operation; provider, downloadable, GUI, and other-build help remains outstanding.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 imported only a trusted GUID-temporary fixture: -NoClobber retained an existing function, -Prefix Probe created the prefixed command, and -PassThru returned the fixture module. It was unloaded and the tree removed.
The page explicitly warns against downloading remote content into Invoke-Expression.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed the irm alias and reproduced the documented OutFile+PassThru empty-file defect with a local file URI under the suite's verified temporary root. HTTP conversion, authentication, proxy, redirect, TLS, and remote content remain outstanding.
The page adds explicit artifact-verification and legacy parser guidance.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed the iwr alias and a local file URI OutFile+PassThru fixture returned one object and a nonempty file below the suite's verified temporary root. HTTP authentication, proxy, redirect, TLS, IE parser, and remote content remain outstanding.
The page treats parsing data as code as a security risk, documents safer alternatives, and explains that -Command binds pipeline strings by value and evaluates each item separately.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 evaluated two fixed in-memory pipeline strings in order and changed a GUID-named script variable in current scope; the variable was removed in finally. No file, profile, network, user, or downloaded input was evaluated.
The page is an availability guide for a custom shorthand, not a claim about a universal alias mapping.
Get-Command irx -All returned no command in the clean Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 session. Installed modules and user/session configuration can still define it elsewhere.
The page is a Windows command-resolution guide rather than a claim that curl is a universal built-in alias.

Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed bare curl resolves to Invoke-WebRequest while exact curl.exe remains separately discoverable. Native curl availability, version, and options remain environment-specific.

The guide emphasizes when direct native invocation is preferable and explains wait, exit-code, stream, and argument-list pitfalls. Microsoft's .NET Process contract supplies the dual-redirected-stream deadlock boundary.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 runtime verification reproduced a blocked capture harness when stdout and stderr were read synchronously in sequence; concurrent asynchronous reads completed the same no-operand usage probe and separated start failure, timeout, exit, stdout and stderr.

Runtime metadata confirmed .NET Framework ProcessStartInfo exposes the Arguments string but not the newer ArgumentList collection. The page separates that API from Start-Process -ArgumentList and requires argument-construction validation before launch.
The page distinguishes the PowerShell alias from the cmd.exe start builtin.
Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed start resolves to Start-Process and every documented alias option matches live metadata. No target process or GUI application was launched.
The guide highlights exact-path input, provider-dependent actions, pipeline binding, and the risk of opening untrusted items.
Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed the ii alias and every documented option against live metadata. No item, file association, provider action, application, or GUI handler was invoked.
The page documents the common ii . workflow while preserving broader provider semantics and trust boundaries.
Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 confirmed ii resolves to Invoke-Item and every documented alias option matches live metadata. No item or GUI handler was invoked.
The guide treats Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 as separately verified runtimes.

Separate Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.8875 and PowerShell 7.6.4 suites confirm edition, version-table keys, command resolution, encoding, question-mark wrappers, and parameter differences. Modules, .NET APIs, remoting endpoints, and arbitrary native applications still require workload-specific migration tests.
